name: Dapagliflozin and metformin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: This fixed combination pairs the sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitor dapagliflozin with metformin. The US label (extended-release tablets) keeps the usual dose at an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 45 or more, does not recommend starting it at eGFR 30 to 45, and contraindicates it below 30 and in end-stage kidney disease because of metformin. Dapagliflozin alone can still be used for kidney and heart protection at lower eGFR (use the components separately).
chip: Do not start if eGFR <45; CI <30

bands.recommendation: Usual dose; maximum dapagliflozin 10 mg and metformin 2,000 mg per day. Check eGFR and volume status before starting (label).

eGFR 45–59: usual dose; consider a lower metformin dose if at risk of hypoperfusion or hypoxemia, and check eGFR every 3–6 months (ADA-KDIGO 2022). eGFR 30–44: do not start; if eGFR falls below 45, weigh benefit and risk of continuing (label). Dapagliflozin is unlikely to lower glucose below 45, but 10 mg once daily still treats CKD and heart failure: use the components separately if needed. If continued at eGFR 30–44, metformin should not exceed 1,000 mg/day (ADA-KDIGO 2022) and dapagliflozin not 10 mg/day: for example one 10 mg/1,000 mg tablet once daily, or the separate components.

Contraindicated below eGFR 30 (metformin; label). Use the components separately: dapagliflozin alone 10 mg once daily for CKD or heart failure (dapagliflozin label: may start at eGFR ≥25, continue below).
Contraindicated (eGFR <30 and end-stage kidney disease; label). Use the components separately: dapagliflozin alone may be continued if already started (dapagliflozin label).

hd.text: Contraindicated in end-stage kidney disease (label). Dapagliflozin alone was not studied in dialysis (see dapagliflozin record).

crrt.text: Not appropriate: metformin contraindicated in severe kidney impairment; hold in acute illness (label).

dialyzable: Metformin: yes, clearance up to 170 mL/min. Dapagliflozin: removal by hemodialysis not studied (label 10).
monitoring: eGFR and volume status before starting and as clinically indicated. Stop at or before iodinated contrast if eGFR <60, liver disease, alcoholism, heart failure or intra-arterial contrast; recheck eGFR at 48 hours. Withhold at least 3 days before surgery or prolonged fasting (ketoacidosis). Genital mycotic infections, urinary tract infection, vitamin B12.

pediatric.usual_dose: Dapagliflozin 5 mg once daily start (with metformin as tolerated); maximum dapagliflozin 10 mg and metformin 2,000 mg per day (label).
pediatric.max_dose: Dapagliflozin 10 mg / metformin 2,000 mg per day.

renal.recommendation: eGFR 45–59: usual. eGFR 30–44: do not start (label applies to all patients).

adult: US product is extended-release only (once daily, morning). Most PH products are immediate-release film-coated tablets (5/500, 5/1000, 10/500, 10/1000 mg), dosed twice daily in their own labeling; kidney thresholds come from the components and are the same, but the US once-daily schedule does not apply to the PH immediate-release tablets.
Component advice in red tiles is taken from the approved dapagliflozin record (start ≥25, continue below 25).

revision_log.change: CrCl 30–59: metformin cap 1,000 mg/day if continued at eGFR 30–44 (ADA-KDIGO 2022). Reviewer's example 'one 10/500 mg tablet twice daily' not used: it would give dapagliflozin 20 mg/day; example given as one 10/1,000 mg tablet once daily.
eGFR 45–59: consider a lower metformin dose with hypoperfusion or hypoxemia; check eGFR every 3–6 months (ADA-KDIGO 2022).
